svg.text: 2 x 2 with wrap, two links a pair
km.Session(cards=[0, 1]) opens two cards; km.Session(card=0, islands=n, shape=...) splits one card into islands, to develop with one card
a group is (first, count), anywhere in the flat ranks
A core holds one table entry an island: its ranks, the link core toward it and the links away. A link core that receives what is not for its
island sends it on; its rooms for what it sends on are kept by the links already travelled, so islands in a circle cannot wait on each other.
The tables are sized by the session. Ran: two P150A joined by four links, and one card split into two to four islands in each of these shapes.
islands are a graph: any shape, a rank any number of links away
the link cores serve four operations, by flat rank or by tensor page
km::write_l1(core, command, rank, address, from, bytes): there when it returns
16 bytes and an add: 11.8 µs across two cards, 1.09 µs inside an island; a split line of three: 8.6 µs one link away, 18.8 µs two
add to a word of a rank
km::add_word(core, command, rank, address, value); with km::posted it does not wait
a posted add: 2.16 µs across two cards; a split line of three: 1.54 µs one link away, 4.04 µs two (experiments/islands/link_ops)
km::write_pages, km::put_bytes: each run of pages another island holds is one line
512 MiB: puts 72.5 GB/s each way with both islands putting; 65,536 keys placed across in 5.99 ms, 0.091 µs a key (09_bucket_sort)
km::read_pages, km::read_bytes: asked of the island that holds them, waited for at the core's port
512 MiB: reads 40.6 to 48.3 GB/s (experiments/islands/islands_pages); a range read across every 1.70 to 1.95 µs
The same call on one island and on many: inside an island it is the NoC write, add or read itself; a link away it is one line to a link core.

svg.text: km::write_pages(writer, command, state, page, 1, scratch) && writes_done()
On one island each call is the local page read or write. Over islands a core reads the pages its island holds from its own DRAM;
each run of pages another island holds is one line across, an ask or a put, waited for at the core's port. The kernel is the same.
a tensor is placed by a hint, and a kernel names the tensor, never the island
what crosses the links, each measured
from the host, a thread, a stream or a graph, to any group of the flat ranks; one completion
a NOP across two cards 4.4 to 5.2 µs; a split line of four: 4.97, 6.06 and 6.25 µs one, two and three links away (25_islands_threads)
a port's send, a reduce's part, a broadcast's block
km::emit to a rank of another island as to any rank
a sum over 238 ranks 167.5 µs against 162.8 on one island of 119 (26_islands_sum, 02_merge_tree's kernels unchanged)
the collectives, over a tree of islands
km::all_gather, all_reduce, reduce_to, broadcast_from; a class's km.all_reduce
256 pages on two cards: all-gather 21.3 µs, all-reduce 180.0 µs; 64 pages on a split ring of four: 27.0 and 331.8 µs
messages.forward to a rank of the other island as to any rank, many messages to a packet
4.7 µs a crossing in a run of round trips; about 4.7 million 64-byte messages a second each way (05_forward)
kmx_fetch, kmx_store of a tensor another island holds, straight between the two DRAMs
64 MiB in 1.13 ms, 59.5 GB/s; the session's own call, session.cross: 512 MiB in 5.35 ms, 100.4 GB/s

svg.text: a reduce or broadcast inside this island
the first rank of each island's part
one part to a rank of island i
the group; its first rank; a local send
a kernel may act by island, in its own words
Ranks are flat and contiguous by island. Between two cards a link runs through the router on an Ethernet tile of each card (row 1 of the
grid); on a split card it is a write over the card's own NoC. Every number is a run on two P150A joined by four links, or on a split card where said.
